art-residencies.headline: Inaugural .ART Award 2026 Open Call
art-residencies.summary: Prize: .ART Domains is accepting applications for the inaugural .ART Award 2026, open remotely with winner announcements taking place in Miami, United States, by the deadline of 1 November 2026. Winners will be revealed on 3 December 2026 during Art Basel Miami. The award is open to artists working in any medium—including painting, sculpture, photography, performance, video, sound, installation, generative art, and NFTs—at any career stage. Geographic or nationality restrictions are not stated. Applicants are expected to submit their artwork along with documentation of their practice and process. Financial breakdown: cash prize amount is not stated; residency placements are included (details not stated); artist fee/stipend is not stated; housing is not stated; travel support is not stated; production support is not stated; application fee is not stated; costs the applicant must cover are not stated. Funding level: funding unclear.

art-residencies.headline: Conveneo Human After All Art Prize for AI-Informed Artistic Practice
art-residencies.summary: Prize hosted by Conveneo, based in the Netherlands (remote submissions), with a deadline of 15 October. The open call seeks artworks that engage artificial intelligence as part of a considered artistic practice shaped by human intention and judgement. Accepted disciplines focus on AI and digital/contemporary art; specific career stage or geographic eligibility restrictions are not stated. The winning artist will receive an award of €5,000. Application fee: free. Production support, exhibition details, and other costs are not stated. Funding level: fully funded (prize award). Information derived from a single social media announcement.

art-residencies.headline: Cullman Center Fellowship 2027–2028 for Scholars and Writers (New York)
art-residencies.summary: Fellowship hosted by the Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers at the New York Public Library, located in New York, USA. Deadline: September 25, 2026. The fellowship runs during the 2027–2028 academic year and is open to scholars, academics, independent researchers, and creative writers whose work benefits directly from access to the research collections at the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building. Fellows are expected to work on their proposed research/writing projects and participate in the center's community. Financial terms: $90,000 stipend; access to NYPL collections provided; housing, travel, and application fees are not stated; funding level: fully funded.
